newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-NOVOTNA ATTRIBUTES LONGEVITY TO DIET AND FITNESS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA ATTRIBUTES LONGEVITY TO DIET AND FITNESS.

text.p: Jana Novotna is something of an elder stateswoman in a sport which increasingly focuses on the achievements of teenagers.
At 28, Novotna is the oldest women's seed at Wimbledon in her 42nd appearance in a Grand Slam tournament.
But age does not wither her and the Czech looked in superb form as she beat Spaniard Gala Leon Garcia in straight sets on Monday to reach the fourth round.
Novotna, who has played at Wimbledon every year since 1986, attributes her longevity to a strict diet and a rigorous exercise regime which includes weight training.
Women's tennis, so often criticised as being too tame, would benefit if other players did the same, the third seed said.
"Looking around the locker room at what players eat and how they take care of themselves I don't think they are doing it in a professional way," Novotna said after her 6-4 6-2 win.
"You have to not only take from your body but also give back."
Novotna has won 12 Grand Slam doubles titles but has yet to take home a singles trophy from one of the big four, despite reaching the quarter-finals or better 16 times.
At Wimbledon she is still remembered chiefly as the woman who wept uncontrollably on the Duchess of Kent's shoulder after throwing away the lead to lose the 1993 final to Steffi Graf in three sets.
Novotna would dearly love the chance to overwrite that memory with victory in the final here but for now she refuses to look that far ahead.
"I am now just really focusing on my next opponent, Mary-Joe Fernandez because she is a very experienced player and that's going to be a really tough one," Novotna said.
"The most important thing is that I am still healthy, that I am physically capable of playing good tennis and that I am still enjoying it. I am not finished yet."
